In observation 23, both the blue jug and the brown wooden chair are visible together from heading 270 (facing -x).

Now I will analyze the exact pixel positions of the jug and chair in observation 23 to compute their positions.

input.command:
python3 -c '
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

# Pose 23:
# From pose 22 (0.183, 2.549), turn -90 (heading 270 = -x), move 0.5:
# x = 0.183 - 0.5 = -0.317, y = 2.549, heading = 270.
# Camera facing -x: forward is -x, right is +y!

arr23 = np.array(Image.open("/work/observations/obs_0023.png"))

# Blue jug:
blue_m = (arr23[:, :, 2] > 150) & (arr23[:, :, 0] < 50) & (arr23[:, :, 1] < 100)
y_j, x_j = np.where(blue_m)
print(f"Jug in obs_0023: x range [{x_j.min()}, {x_j.max()}], cx = {x_j.mean():.1f}, bottom y = {y_j.max()}")

# Chair:
chair_m = (arr23[:, :, 0] > 70) & (arr23[:, :, 0] < 160) & (arr23[:, :, 1] > 30) & (arr23[:, :, 1] < 90) & (arr23[:, :, 2] < 35) & (np.arange(512)[None, :] > 300)
y_c, x_c = np.where(chair_m)
print(f"Chair in obs_0023: x range [{x_c.min()}, {x_c.max()}], cx = {x_c.mean():.1f}, bottom y = {y_c.max()}")
'
